problem: Autoregressive navigation world models (e.g. NWM) recursively feed their own predictions back, so noise accumulates over long horizons (perceptual drift), and predicted views drift from the agent's motion (geometric drift). Prior geometry fixes need costly 3D supervision such as depth or point clouds.
motivation: Planning through a world model needs simulated futures that stay stable over long horizons and remain faithful to the geometry induced by the agent's actions. Predicting distant anchors first, as classical planners and humans do, shortens the recursive chain. Anchors also give two views of the same rollout, which enables bidirectional epipolar constraints without 3D supervision.
key_idea: Predict sparse future anchors first, then fill in intermediate frames per chunk conditioned on past context and the future anchor, using bidirectional epipolar attention masks derived from the past and future views.
insight: Anchor-guided rollout alone reduces perceptual drift: swapping AR for anchor inference improves LPIPS and FID at all horizons (16s FID 140.3 to 76.9). It gives only a modest geometric gain. The geometric gain depends on AC-DiT's internals: future anchor, epipolar mask and chunking are complementary, and only the full model gives the best average Sampson error (56.37 vs 60.76 to 64.31). Epipolar masking without the future anchor degrades to a weaker line-based constraint and is worse.
method: Anchor-guided rollout: first predict sparse anchors directly from the observed history and the action subsequence (a fixed interval apart), then generate the intermediate frames of each chunk between consecutive anchors, so errors do not compound recursively.
Chunk generation with bidirectional conditioning: each chunk is conditioned on past context frames, the future anchor, the forward actions, and the inverse actions defined from the anchor backward.

Bidirectional epipolar masking: LoFTR matches plus RANSAC fundamental matrices give epipolar lines in the goal frame from the past and future views. Their intersection is discretized on the 14x14 token grid into binary cross-attention masks. Rows with no valid match stay unmasked, and reliability gating from inlier counts and EMA temporal smoothing are applied.

AC-DiT: extends the pretrained CDiT/XL with past cross-attention (PA), future cross-attention (FA) and chunk temporal attention (chunk length K=3). It adds a future-side scalar embedding of inverse action and future time offset, with zero-initialized gates so pretrained behavior is preserved at the start of fine-tuning.
Training: standard denoising MSE loss on target chunks, fine-tuned from the NWM CDiT/XL checkpoint (AdamW, batch 4, lr 8e-6). Masks act as attention masks, with no auxiliary 3D loss.
Planning: the unchanged NWM planners (CEM and NoMaD) rank 32 sampled 4-second trajectories using the improved world model.

setting.backbone: AC-DiT (CDiT/XL from NWM, fine-tuned with new anchor/epipolar modules) with SD VAE tokenizer
setting.training_data: Fine-tuned on RECON, SCAND, HuRoN (low-res 160x120 public version) and TartanDrive; LoFTR matches computed offline; starts from the NWM checkpoint (which was also trained with Ego4D)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (224x224) history plus actions
setting.action_space: planar continuous actions in R^3 (relative motion); planning samples 32 candidate trajectories over 4s
setting.privileged: none at test time (anchors are predicted; LoFTR matching is applied on predicted or observed frames)

Split names are set to 'test' by assumption (the paper does not state them).
results: DR-NWM beats NWM and EgoWM on LPIPS, DreamSim and FID at all horizons on all four datasets, with the gap growing at longer horizons (e.g. RECON 16s FID 76.9 vs NWM 112.7). It also gets lower epipolar distance and Sampson error in nearly all settings, and lower MEt3R at all skips. With unchanged CEM and NoMaD planners, it lowers ATE, FDE and RPE (RECON CEM ATE 3.18 to 2.78).
limitations: Geometric supervision depends on noisy LoFTR/RANSAC matches, so masks are disabled when matches are insufficient, and a segmentation model is needed to filter sky and dynamic regions.
Anchors are still predicted directly and can be wrong; the fixed anchor interval and chunk length (K=3) are heuristics, and the low-resolution HuRoN version weakens comparability.
Planning is evaluated only offline on RECON and SCAND with gains shrinking at high sample counts; no real-robot or closed-loop test.
